name: Moltis
vibe_summary: A security-first, single-binary Rust agent server that positions itself as the hardened alternative to OpenClaw. Sandboxed execution, auditable codebase, and no plugin marketplace supply-chain risk.
best_for: Security-conscious self-hosters wanting a hardened agent server
Users who prefer a single auditable Rust binary over Node/Python stacks
Home-lab setups on Mac Mini, Raspberry Pi, or personal servers

You need the massive community and docs footprint of OpenClaw
You prefer TypeScript/Python for easy hacking and contributions

Single Rust binary with no Node/npm runtime or supply-chain surface
Deliberately auditable core (~7.5K line agent runner) with isolated unsafe code

Younger project with less battle-testing and fewer third-party integrations

overview_markdown:
Moltis is a security-first personal agent server written in Rust, distributed as a single binary with no Node.js or npm runtime. It explicitly positions itself against OpenClaw with a comparison table, emphasizing sandboxed container execution for every command, keys that never leave the host, and an auditable architecture: a ~7.5K-line agent runner and model interface, ~19K lines of providers, and a ~270K-line workspace across 59 modular crates with 470+ test files. Unsafe code is confined to FFI and precompiled runtime boundaries.

Feature-wise it is broad: multi-provider LLMs, voice, persistent memory with cross-session recall, edit checkpoints, scheduling, Telegram/Signal/Discord/WhatsApp/Teams channels, browser automation, MCP servers, SSH or node-backed remote execution, and managed deploy keys with host pinning. Notably, it deliberately avoids a plugin marketplace, framing that as a supply-chain security decision rather than a gap.

Recent commits show an active and serious security posture: fixes for sandbox session-ID collisions that could alias containers across sessions, and a hardening of remote node execution (versioned argv protocol, default-deny allowlists, admin gating, credential binding) with credited responsible disclosure. Compared to OpenClaw, Moltis trades ecosystem size and community momentum for a hardened, minimal-trust architecture aimed at self-hosters who prioritize auditability.
